beta_new:
The opening lead is an easy angling ramp at fourth-class level to a chockstone, then a jam crack past chiseled holds to a bolted ledge.

Next the crack widens into a squeeze chimney slot pocked with holes left by an old pipe ladder; a big cam gives security there.
Ascend the right-hand wall of the obvious corner standing behind a big fir. Dicey easy-grade moves lead up to the initial bolt, and two more bolts take you to the top.
Climb as far as the first bolt of Astral Projection, then make a longer move sideways to the bolt at the slab's outer edge before edging back toward the anchors.
Work up the shallow corner leaning right beside Thug Route to the tree.

moves.from: A small rack of nuts, small cams and TCUs is all it takes.

value.text: A small rack of nuts, small cams and TCUs.

beta_new: Start beside the big roof, go around its left side, then trend up and right over the stained seep line and some ledges to the three-bolt headwall.

moves.from: Small gear to about a #1.5 cam supplements.

value.text: Small gear up to about a #1.5 cam.

beta_new: Move left beyond a bolt, then wedge your fingers up a thin crack for about forty feet; two hard fingertip laybacks are the crux.
Pull on good holds up the face to a runout leftward traverse, then step onto the low-angle upper wall and cruise to the anchors.

Begin with the lowest part of Rip Curl, then move left over flakes to a flared offwidth. Expect a long fight with stacked hands and arm bars on the crux section.

Higher, the crack tightens to fist-and-hand width and gives way to a strenuous lieback and jamming stretch. Bring plenty of big gear and tape your hands.
Reach the tree belay, then pass the bolt and enter the shallow corner. From its top, edge rightward into a thin, sustained seam and belay; easier ground above lets you bail rightward.

Meander up a slab, round a roof by its east side with a #1.5 cam, then belay from a shelf under a shallow groove.

The groove takes two bolts; then angle up-left to a crack, follow it out, and shift over to another one. A final crack reaches easy ground, where you leave to the east.

A steep slab in two pitches. The first has thin moves protected by two bolts and creative gear placements, belaying at chains; six bolts follow up the headwall, with the crux just below the top belay. Small cams add a placement low down.
Take the dihedral shared with North Roof, then peel off leftward where a shelf slopes and pass a lone bolt to reach a bolted anchor.

Start on five bolts beside Endless Crack, then take that route's second pitch to a stance next to Kite Slab.

Next, step out rightward to a bolt, climb the steeply angled slab past two further bolts to a horn under a roof, and push through the roof where a wedged block fills the slot. Finish through a chimney.
Climb a short crack, then continue on clean face rock through four bolts, finishing at twin anchors.
A long crack system along the wall's right edge that takes five or six pitches. Head toward the large tree against the sky; the upper pitches trend left to reach it.

The opening pitch is a sixty-foot face section that is mostly unprotected, with a few harder moves near its top before a bolted belay.

The second pitch trends up and left over four bolts toward a distinct roof; the crux sits at the fourth bolt, and the roof is turned on its left side to a ledge with anchors.

Begin beneath a broken corner, then trend leftward through two ring bolts into the crack system that angles rightward. Three more bolts follow, with a thin, steep crux; an extra medium cam or large wire helps in the crack under the headwall.

moves.from: an extra medium cam or large wire helps in the crack under the headwall

value.text: An extra medium cam or large wire for the crack under the headwall.

beta_new: Start near a big Douglas fir and follow the bolts through a pair of roofs, finishing alongside the V-shaped slot on its right-hand edge.
Straight up the wall centre on five bolts, ending at a lone anchor at the wall's top.

From the saddle at about 13,000 ft, follow the ridge crest and ledges on its right side. Near 13,300 ft the route crosses a small gap in the ridge, the "leap of faith" - a short step across rather than a true leap - onto narrow, exposed ledges beyond. Around 13,400 ft you reach a steep band of greenish rock (the "green wall"); climb it on Class 3-4 ledges, testing every hold. Above, the route works up a series of gullies and ledges on the west side of the ridge, marked by cairns; staying on the cairned line keeps the difficulty at Class 3-4, while wandering usually lands you on steeper, looser ground. Above about 13,900 ft the angle eases and you walk to the summit. Note landmarks on the way up, because the upper route is easy to lose on the way down.

A zigzagging crack-and-corner line that bends over five roofs. Begin from a flake on the right and step left where the largest roof hangs.

The next pitch ascends the dihedral and crosses a roof on a fist-sized crack.

moves.from: ; protection runs from small wires up to medium cams

beta_new: Follow a hand crack that leans, out at the westernmost end of the formation.

moves.from: Cams up to about 3.5 inches cover it.

beta_new: Thin, technical climbing on the wall's right side where reach matters. Above the roof the crux relies on tiny pebble pinches. Four bolts lead to lowering anchors on cold shuts.
Begin with an easy 5.6 crack that ends on a flake, then pull up through a sequence of pockets past a handful of old fixed pegs. It is somewhat runout, so expect to lean on the fixed gear.

Scramble up the ramp, then angle leftward on 5.9 ground to the first bolt. The difficulty builds steadily to a tricky crux past the fourth bolt, after which easier climbing reaches the ridge. Carry some wires and a #1 cam for the start.

moves.from: Carry some wires and a #1 cam for the start.

value.text: Some wires and a #1 cam for the start.

beta_new: A lengthy bolted face climb with sustained difficulty up the steep right-hand side of the gully, in three pitches. Begin high in the chimney below a curving crack.
From the neighbouring route's rappel station, trend rightward through a series of dihedrals past scattered fixed gear to a belay below a black groove. Follow that groove to the top; it is runout.

Begin back of a fir tree, to the right of the large dihedral, then crank up and rightward past six bolts to double cold-shut anchors. Holds are mostly good, but reaching the anchors without a dynamic lunge to the ridge is awkward.

Climb a three-bolt slab to a ledge, then move straight to a mantle that lands you at a rest above a roof. Haul over the large roof on big holds and finish via another bulge, or angle right for an easier exit. Ten bolts in all.
An easy slab leads to a corner beneath the large roof. Grab a rest there, then power through the roof, where several separate 5.12 cruxes await on fine rock. Ten bolts total.
The big dihedral resembles a numeral 7. Climb up it and then get around the roof by going left.

moves.from: Gear to about five inches is wanted.

beta_new: Steep slab work with one hard smear move opens the route, then the upper headwall is somewhat easier; the pitch ends on a narrow ledge with anchors.
An arching crack up the left edge of the wall. Near the top, step back leftward onto a finger-sized crack for the crux; a 3.5 cam is useful.
Follow the first hundred feet of the neighbouring route and belay, then leave it leftward and ascend the slab via two bolts, curving back to the right.

A long buttress route of fourteen pitches. Early pitches climb unprotected slab and cracks; the fourth heads leftward on a very thin crack through a steep headwall, then a thin bolted slab to a groove.

Upper pitches follow grooves, a good left-facing corner and slab leading into a system of cracks, mostly at 5.8 to 5.9.
Start like the neighbouring route, but veer off rightward at the first bolt, get past a burly bulge, and layback through a roof. At the final bolt, choose either anchor. Five bolts.
A three-bolt line up the vertical face to the right of the neighbouring route. Clip the first bolt with a stick, carry small gear for the upper section, and belay on that route's ledge.

moves.from: carry small gear for the upper section

value.text: Small gear for the upper section.

beta_new: A layback section and thin crack in the line east of the arete. It is easily toproped from the anchors of Brain Cloud.

moves.from: Nuts and small cams protect it

beta_new:
Start along the left edge of the big flake leaning on the face; a few moves of 5.9 on crumbly flakes lead onto a gentle, runout slab and bolted belay on top of the flake.

The second pitch follows the water streak clipping a series of bolts to a stance under a small roof. Add a short hand-crack third pitch, with gear to 3 inches, to reach the summit.

value.text: Gear to 3 in for the optional third pitch.

beta_new: From the gully, go up an easy chimney, exit rightward onto an angled ledge system and belay there. The route itself follows the colorful yellow wall overhead, clipping five bolts to the lowering anchors.
